Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Australia's reply. Jasprit Bumrah and Co. have made their way out to the middle. It will be Usman Khawaja and the debutant, Nathan McSweeney to open the innings for Australia. The Indian skipper Jasprit Bumrah has the new ball in hand. Away we go...
... FOURTH INNINGS ....

Right then, as per Mark Nicholas on air, we have 25 minutes of play left today, including the 30 minutes of added time. After being on the field for almost five sessions without much rest, the Aussie openers will be tired. Jasprit Bumrah has sensed the opportunity to have a crack at them. 450 is the highest fourth-innings total in Australia in Tests, and that gives a clear indication of the mammoth task ahead for the hosts. Their primary aim, though, will be to see off the remaining phase of the day unscathed. Can they hold firm? Back in a bit to find out.

Virat Kohli is in for a chat with Adam Gilchrist. He says that Anushka, his wife has been right there by his side. Adds that she knows what goes behind the scenes. Mentions that he takes a lot of pride in playing for his country and is really happy to get a ton here in front of his family.

India have declared! As anticipated, the declaration came immediately after Virat Kohli reached his century. A look of relief is evident on Kohli's face as he walks off the field. The innings had a steady rhythm with Sundar and Kohli in control, but Nitish Kumar Reddy's arrival brought a clear shift in intent. Kohli soon accelerated to match the tempo and raced to his century. It's been quite a day for India - first, Yashasvi Jaiswal brought up his hundred, and now Virat Kohli has followed suit with his own to set Australia a target of 534 runs. For Australia, while the misery of being in the field close to 5 sessions is over, they now face the tricky task of surviving the remainder of the day.

FOUR! THERE IT IS! NUMBER 81! HUNDRED FOR KOHLI! 30th Test ton for him. His 9th against Australia. One of the most important knocks of his Test career! The Optus Stadium erupts in huge applause for the man of the moment! Coming to the delivery, Marnus Labuschagne lands it flat and full in length, just outside leg, Virat Kohli shuffles across and sits on his knee before sweeping it powerfully to the gap between deep fine and deep backward square leg. The fielder from deep backward square leg puts in a full-stretched dive, even gets fingertips of his right on the ball but eventually parries it on the ropes. Kohli finally raises his bat in the air and soaks in all the appreciation from the crowd.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back! The umpires and players are punctual. Australian players take their fielding positions. Virat Kohli, unbeaten on 40, and Washington Sundar on 14 to resume their innings for India. It will be the Australian skipper, Pat Cummins who will kick off the proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... DAY 3, SESSION 3 ...

As the session progressed, there were signs of some spin as well for Lyon who had just outfoxed Pant. But with Kohli well settled, he looked in confidence and peppered the field with some extravagant strokes. With Sundar playing the perfect second fiddle, the duo kept the scoreboard ticking, methodically expanding India's cushion and dashing the collapse further. India currently holds a very healthy lead of 405 runs with 5 wickets still to spare. Coming into the final session, Australia's aim would be to bundle India out and bank a couple of days to chase. India, on the other hand, would like to bat through the day and take the game further away from the claws of the hosts. Stay tuned, as an exciting post-Tea session will begin at 7.20 am GMT.

Though the pitch had begun showing signs of wear with occasional variable bounce creeping in, batting conditions remained largely favorable in the first hour. However, the mounting pressure from Australia's disciplined bowling took its toll. Yashasvi Jaiswal, perhaps caught between caution and aggression, fell trying to force the pace. This triggered an astonishing collapse as India's commanding position of 313/2 crumbled to a vulnerable 321/5. Three wickets tumbled in just about four overs, though the Indian batters were masters of their own downfall and would rue their rash shot selection.

This session after Lunch moved the contest at a brisk pace. Despite India's comfortable position with a healthy lead already, Australia found their breakthrough immediately as Josh Hazlewood struck with the very first delivery of the session, dismissing the well-set Devdutt Padikkal. This wicket seemed to energize the Australian seamers, who tightened their lines and lengths considerably, attempting to plug the run flow.

TEA, DAY 3 - Session Summary - 26 overs, 84 runs, 4 wickets. A session of two halves, to be fair, and a much better session for Australia. The bowlers dominated the first hour, followed by a resilient stand between Kohli and Sundar for the sixth wicket. In the current scenario, India have lead 5 sessions so far versus two sessions dominated by the Aussies with this one being shared by both sides.

In Test cricket, from a bowling side's perspective, when you take the second new ball and fail to make it count, it can play straight into the hands of the batting side. The Aussies have not started well, conceding 20 runs from the first 4 overs of the second new ball. With the pitch not showing any signs of deterioration so far, Australia will need to bowl with discipline during this crucial phase. As long as the new ball remains hard, any lack of control could see the runs leaking at a healthy rate, which would only add to Australia's troubles. Do join us back at 5 am GMT for the start of the second session. Cheers!

The pair provided a steady start, with Jaiswal reaching his 4th Test century and his first on Australian soil. The 201-run opening stand was brought to an end by Mitchell Starc as he dismissed Rahul on 77. Having reached his ton, Jaiswal seemed to lose a bit of composure, but he continued to ride his luck. The closest Australia came to dismissing Jaiswal today was through a mix-up between him and Rahul, but Cummins couldn't knock down the stumps at the bowling end, despite Jaiswal having given up. Coming in at number three, Devdutt Padikkal has offered a better account of himself in the middle, and together with Jaiswal, they have further solidified India's position.

Another session bossed by India in this Test! Having started the day with a lead of 218 runs, they have scored 103 runs from 27 overs for the loss of a solitary wicket. Commentary.Commentary: All set for this 'Moving Day' to get going at the Optus Stadium! It is warm and sunny out there, with the mercury expected to clock in the mid-30s as the day progresses. The two umpires walk out to the middle and the Australian players take their respective fielding positions. Yashasvi Jaiswal, approaching the triple figures, along with KL Rahul unbeaten on 62 are the overnight batters for India. The tourists lead by 218 runs with all ten wickets in hand. And it will be Josh Hazlewood (10-5-9-0) to open the attack for Australia on Day 3. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Russel Arnold and Wasim Akram share their observations ahead of Day 3. Russel notes that yesterday was hot, and with even hotter conditions expected today, the pitch will continue to bake. He highlights that while there’s still plenty of grass visible, some of it has started browning due to the heat. He also points out the presence of a few rough patches and cracks running across the surface, which are likely to widen as the match progresses. Wasim, however, believes the cracks may not open up completely today due to the remaining grass, suggesting they could become more pronounced tomorrow.

The temperature at Perth is expected to be a bit more warm, which will surely expand those small visible cracks as we progress into the third day. It will ultimately make batting a bit challenging as the game progresses with the pitch’s wear and tear. But for now, it’s all on the shoulders of the Aussie pace trio to make early inroads, strike through the top order and prevent India from broadening up the lead considerably. Will the Indian openers survive the first crucial hour, or will Australia's determined bowlers find their breakthrough on this potentially decisive third day? We will find out together as the first ball will be bowled at 2.20 am GMT.

While the batters had a disappointing day at business on the opening day, the bowling card for the second day looks pretty sorry-looking. But to be very fair to them, the Aussie bowlers bowled their hearts out and also went past the edges on multiple occasions. Especially, Josh Hazlewood who looked the most threatening of all, giving absolutely nothing. But alas, they couldn’t create any inroad and remained wicketless. The reduced seam movement as compared to the first innings and instances where the ball didn't carry to the slips, coupled with Usman Khawaja grassing a catch and a missed run-out chance, all have only added to their frustration.

Very fair to say, that India hold firm control of this contest, at least for now as KL Rahul and Yashasvi Jaiswal, the openers have batted being unblemished for two entire sessions. Yes, some might say things slowed down a bit, especially Jaiswal notching his slowest Test half-century, taking 123 deliveries, which was highly uncharacteristic of his own. But what is important here for India is, they have all ten wickets in the bank. Also, KL Rahul had a point to prove as he entered this series with a sudden dip in form but has grabbed this opportunity with both hands in fine fashion.

The Perth Test has flipped the cricketing script dramatically. Where the opening day saw seamers from both sides wreak havoc with 17 wickets tumbling, only for Day 2 to completely go dry with just 3 dismissals. If you ever needed proof of why cricket's called the game of uncertainties, this was it. This Test has moved at a decent pace so far and on that note, we welcome you all to the coverage of Day 3 of this first Test in the Border-Gavaskar Trophy 2024/25 from the iconic Optus Stadium.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, with three days still to play, India find themselves firmly in the driver’s seat and their objective will be to effectively bat Australia out of the contest. Conditions on Day 3 are expected to feature slightly higher temperatures compared to Day 2, which could bake the pitch further. As the day progresses, the visible cracks might widen, making batting increasingly challenging. Australia will be mindful of the fact that in recent Tests, India have been prone to collapses. They will believe that if they can break this stand early, they can build on it and claw their way back into the game. An exciting day lies ahead, with the first ball on Day 3 set for 2.20 am GMT but as always our build-up will begin much earlier. See you then. Cheers!

Chances were few and far between, but Australia did manage to create a couple of opportunities. One came in the form of a tough catch of Jaiswal, which was put down by Usman Khawaja. On the very next ball, a potential run-out chance was missed, as a wayward throw from Steven Smith failed to find Rahul in trouble. These moments of missed chances were pivotal, and as the day wore on, India capitalized on them to end the day with a lead of 218 runs. To be fair, Pat Cummins and Co. could consider themselves unlucky, as they tried everything and managed to beat the bat on quite a few occasions, but the breakthrough eluded them.

Starc and Hazlewood’s resilience raised questions about whether the softer, older ball or an easing pitch was making batting more manageable. The answer came soon enough as Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul took to the crease. They handled the new ball with relative comfort, facing far less lateral movement than what was evident on the first morning. As the scoreboard reflects, sessions 2 and 3 were bossed by India, with the Australian bowlers struggling to make inroads.

Australia began the day trailing by 83 runs with three wickets in hand, relying on Alex Carey to narrow the deficit. However, Jasprit Bumrah struck with his first ball, dismissing Carey and completing his 11th Test five-wicket haul. India seemed set to wrap things up quickly, but Mitchell Starc showed remarkable grit, facing 112 balls. He and Josh Hazlewood formed the innings’ highest partnership, adding 25 runs and frustrating the bowlers. The visitors eventually broke through, taking a 46-run lead.

Well, what a stark contrast from the drama of Day 1! The second day unfolded with much more serenity, but at the end of it, India have firmly kept their grip on the Test. Few would have anticipated such a turnaround after the chaos of the opening day, where 17 wickets tumbled on a lively, green surface. In comparison, only three wickets fell on Day 2, as the pitch began to show signs of easing out, making batting a relatively more manageable task.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the final session. The umpires and players are punctual and the Australian fielders take their positions. Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul to resume their innings for India. And it will be Pat Cummins to kick off the final session with the ball. Here we go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

Did the movement just die off the pitch or did the batters apply themselves well? Can say, both, for now, at least. The sudden metamorphosis in the conditions has been striking - from yesterday's seam-bowling haven to today's more balanced surface with the ball not seaming much. The opening pair's unbroken partnership has steadily expanded India's lead to 130 runs, presenting a stark contrast to the clatter of wickets witnessed on day one. With the final session left in Day 2, can Australia turn around its fortunes and strike a roaring comeback? Or will India manage to get a comfortable lead? Join us for the post-Tea session which starts at 7.20 am GMT. Stay tuned.

This shift in conditions was first hinted at during Australia's stubborn last-wicket partnership, and the trend has continued with India's openers showing remarkable resilience. For India, Yashasvi Jaiswal who perished on a duck, redeemed himself with a solid unbeaten knock while KL Rahul carried on the momentum in the second innings as well. Australia also utilized Nathan Lyon, but there was no turn whatsoever and Labuschange was also used towards the end of the session but they didn't get much assistance as the pitch eased out with the progression.

With the pitch easing up a bit to bat on, the Indian openers began on a positive note. KL Rahul and Jaiswal both effectively rotated the strike and kept the scorecard ticking. Although there was some lateral movement on offer for the seamers with the new ball, they caused minimal trouble and were negotiated with caution early on. The Australian pace attack, despite cycling through all their seamers within the first ten overs in search of a breakthrough, couldn't replicate the opening day's dominance.

TEA, DAY 2 - Session Summary - 26 overs, 84 runs, 0 wickets. A positive session for India as they go unblemished in the post-Lunch session after beginning their innings with a lead of 46 runs. On the other hand, the Australian bowlers would be feeling a bit exasperated as they have used all their bowling resources, but haven't broken through as yet. With this, India have led three sessions so far versus Australia dominating two.

Stays around the wicket for the last ball of the session and serves it short, on middle and leg, Rahul rocks on the back foot and stabs it down on the leg side. India go to TEA on 84/0, leading by 130 runs!
